misconceptions.description: Assuming constructivist learning means the designer should remove all structure
misconceptions.trigger: learner claims constructivist environments should be completely open and unguided
misconceptions.feedback: Constructivist learning still needs structure. The difference is that the structure supports exploration, discussion, and revision rather than one-way transmission.

misconceptions.description: Reducing the ZPD to anything that feels hard
misconceptions.trigger: learner identifies impossible tasks or trivial tasks as being in the ZPD
misconceptions.feedback: The ZPD is not just 'hard work.' It is the range where a learner can succeed with support but not yet alone.

misconceptions.description: Treating scaffolding as support that should never be removed
misconceptions.trigger: learner argues that supports should remain unchanged even after mastery improves
misconceptions.feedback: Scaffolding is temporary. As the learner gains independence, the supports should fade so the learner takes over more of the cognitive work.
